# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 100 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 100 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_100_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 17

**1** "Now, Lord," I said, "explain to me also the virgins." "Do you not understand," he said, "what the virgins are?" **2** "No, Lord," I answered. "These twelve virgins," he said, "are spirits. **3** But why are they not all called by the same name? Listen. **4** The four corner virgins are the mightier among them and also lead the rest — **5** because anyone who bears their names shall enter the kingdom of God. **6** But the names of the weaker ones who stand between them — **7** whoever bears the name of these also and the names of those who preside over them, shall also enter the kingdom of God." **8** "Do the virgins have any power?" I asked. **9** "Yes, they do have power," he said. "Indeed all of these holy spirits have power, and those who bear their names cannot do otherwise than act in accordance with those spirits. **10** But see what the women are who are clothed in the black garments — who are they?" **11** "These also," he said, "are twelve in number, sisters of these. Their names are: Unbelief, Intemperance, Disobedience, Deceit, Sorrow, Wickedness, Licentiousness, Bitter-temperedness, Lying, and Hatred. **12** Whoever among the servants of God bear these names shall not enter the kingdom of God, but shall be cast out." **13** "But the stones that were rejected and not fitted into the tower — who are they?" **14** "These are the dry ones," he said, "those who have the names of the wicked women. They cannot be fitted in because they are rough and full of marks from the wicked women."

---

*EMET: the twelve virgins as spirits whose names one "bears" = the wearing of virtues as a spiritual identity. The black-garmented women's names precisely mirror the list in ch. 83.*
